title: U.S. House · Nebraska's 2nd District

context.text: The seat is open because incumbent Rep. Don Bacon (R) did not seek re-election. Brinker Harding was the only candidate to make the Republican primary ballot after Don Bacon and Brett Lindstrom did not enter. Denise Powell won a seven-way Democratic primary with 38.8% of the vote, narrowly ahead of John Cavanaugh (36.4%), with Crystal Rhoades, Kishla Askins and Melanie Williams also running. Cook Political Report's Partisan Voter Index rated the district D+3 based on presidential voting patterns.

summary.text: Denise Powell is an Omaha business owner and mother who co-founded Women Who Run Nebraska, a political action committee that supports women running for office, and has advocated on public-education and healthcare issues. She has not previously held public office and won the May 12, 2026 Democratic primary for the open 2nd District seat. She is running on lowering costs, protecting reproductive healthcare, and opposing what she describes as abuses of executive power.

background.text: Describes herself as a working mother and small-business owner; a local news report says she lives in Central Omaha with her husband and two children.
According to Ballotpedia, she is a former corporate communications director and partner at an architecture firm.
Says she has spent the past decade advocating in Nebraska for reproductive healthcare access and strong public schools, and has advocated for Nebraska schools for 16 years.

Co-founded Women Who Run Nebraska in 2017 after attending the Women's March in Washington, D.C.; the group is a political action committee that recruits and supports women running for office, and she later led it.
Says she helped rally physicians and patients against a proposed total abortion ban in Nebraska and collected signatures for a ballot measure to protect abortion access.
Has spoken publicly about a near-fatal ectopic pregnancy about 14 years ago, which she says shapes her views on reproductive healthcare.
Announced her candidacy for Nebraska's 2nd District, saying she had never served in public office. Nebraska Examiner describes her as a business and nonprofit consultant.
Won the May 12, 2026 Democratic primary with 38.8% of the vote, ahead of State Sen. John Cavanaugh (36.4%) and Douglas County District Court Clerk Crystal Rhoades (14.1%).

priorities.text: Lowering costs for families on groceries, energy, housing and childcare.
Protecting and expanding access to reproductive healthcare, including abortion, contraception and IVF.
Protecting Social Security and Medicare, including opposing benefit cuts and raising the retirement age.
Congressional oversight of the executive branch and ethics reform, including banning congressional stock trading and term limits.

positions.summary: Supports restoring nationwide abortion rights and expanding access to contraception and fertility treatments.
positions.quote: Protect abortion rights for Nebraska women by fighting to restore Roe v. Wade into law nationwide.

positions.summary: Supports creating a Medicare-like public option and letting Medicare negotiate more prescription-drug prices.
positions.quote: Work to create a Medicare-like public option that gives every American the choice of affordable coverage while protecting private insurance for those who want it.

positions.summary: Supports universal background checks and red-flag laws.
positions.quote: Save lives from gun violence by ensuring universal background checks to prevent convicted felons and gang members from obtaining guns, red flag laws to keep guns out of the hands of domestic abusers, and fund community violence intervention programs.

positions.summary: Her campaign site calls for stopping what she calls Trump's illegal tariffs, while also supporting targeted tariffs on specific imports like beef and soybeans.
positions.quote: Stop Trump’s illegal tariffs to help bring down the costs of items Nebraska families need every day.

positions.summary: Her 2026 campaign website lists expanding clean energy production among her priorities for lowering costs while protecting the environment.
positions.quote: Expand clean energy production to bring down costs in the short term while protecting our environment in the long run.

summary.text: Brinker Harding is an Omaha City Council member since 2017, a commercial real estate professional, and a former Chief of Staff to Omaha Mayor Hal Daub. He is the Republican nominee for the open 2nd District seat. He is running on economic growth, reducing federal spending, and border security, citing his record balancing Omaha's city budget.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he is a fourth-generation Omahan, married to Rebecca, with two daughters, Elizabeth and Grace.
BallotReady lists a high school diploma from Westside High School (1979) and a bachelor's degree from the University of Kansas (1984).

From 1995 to 2000, he served as Chief of Staff and Director of Economic Development to Omaha Mayor Hal Daub; his campaign website says the office formed public-private partnerships for riverfront parks, the CHI Convention Center and the Dodge Expressway.
Worked in commercial real estate at Colliers International; BallotReady also lists a vice president role at Grubb & Ellis.
Has served on the Omaha City Council representing District 6 since 2017; his term runs through 2029.

According to his campaign website, as a council member he has voted to lower Omaha's property tax levy three times and worked on projects including the Gene Leahy Mall, a library at 72nd and Dodge, and the Heartwood Preserve development.
Describes himself as a business leader who developed public-private partnerships to grow Omaha's economy.
Was the only candidate on the May 12, 2026 Republican primary ballot for the open 2nd District seat.

priorities.text: Making America more affordable by growing the economy, lowering gas and grocery prices, and cutting inflation.
Congressional accountability: term limits, banning congressional stock trading, and halting congressional pay during government shutdowns.
Border security, including deporting people in the country illegally who commit violent crimes.
Reducing federal spending to address the national debt.

positions.summary: Says he supported a record pay raise for Omaha police officers on the City Council and cites Omaha's falling violent-crime rate as a result.
positions.quote: In Omaha, we didn't defund the police. We gave our heroes the record pay raise they deserve. As a result, we have driven Omaha's violent crime rate to 40-year lows.

positions.summary: His 2026 campaign website says he would protect Social Security, Medicaid and Medicare for seniors, veterans, single mothers and people with disabilities, but not for people in the country illegally or able-bodied adults.
positions.quote: Protect critical programs like Social Security, Medicaid, and Medicare for single moms, veterans, the elderly, and disabled – NOT illegal immigrants or able-bodied adults

record.text: Says he has balanced Omaha's city budget every year while on the City Council.

candidates.name: Eric Michael Foreman

summary.text: Eric Michael Foreman is the Libertarian Party nominee, with a career in property management. He describes himself as a blue-collar worker and not a career politician. His campaign centers on ending U.S. involvement in foreign wars, cutting taxes for people earning under $200,000, and opposing what he calls government overreach.

background.text: According to Ballotpedia, his career experience includes working in property management.
Describes himself as a blue-collar worker who has "worked honest jobs" and is not a career politician.
Says he has raised a family "the hard way—without handouts or shortcuts."
Advanced from the May 12, 2026 Libertarian Party primary to the general election ballot.

priorities.text: Ending U.S. financial commitments to foreign wars.
Lower taxes for people earning under $200,000 a year, and exempting a paid-off primary home from taxation.
Protecting constitutional rights, including the right to self-defense and free speech.

candidates.researchNotes: Statements from his 2026 Ballotpedia survey. A campaign website (foremantakebackourhouse.com) with a platform page exists but was not mined for further statements; no news questionnaire found.

statements.quote: Lower taxes for the Lower 85% of Americans that make less than 200k a year, cut the waste, prosecute the fraud, and let hardworking Nebraskans keep more of what they earn.
statements.context: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

statements.quote: Liberty first. Protect the Constitution, Your right to Self defense, free speech, and the right to live free from government meddling in our lives, faith, and families.
statements.context: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey
